meaning.en: To feel jealous, especially over a lover's attention to someone else.
meaning.zh: 在感情上嫉妒。

examples.zh: 他看到女朋友和别的男生聊天，忍不住吃醋了。
examples.en: He couldn't help feeling jealous when he saw his girlfriend chatting with another guy.

examples.zh: 你别吃醋，我只是在帮同事的忙。
examples.en: Don't be jealous, I'm just helping a colleague.

usage.en: Verb-object; mostly about romantic jealousy. Vinegar's sourness stands for the sour feeling of jealousy; can be used playfully.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，多指情爱上的嫉妒。醋的酸味比喻嫉妒的心情，也常用于开玩笑。

meaning.en: To dismiss an employee from a job.
meaning.zh: 解雇，辞退。

examples.zh: 他三天两头迟到，被老板炒了鱿鱼。
examples.en: He was always late and the boss gave him the sack.

examples.zh: 公司业绩不好，一下子炒了十几个人的鱿鱼。
examples.en: The firm did badly and fired a dozen people at once.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; the object can be inserted (炒他鱿鱼). When cooked, squid curls up like a rolled bedroll, as workers did when told to pack up and leave.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语。鱿鱼一炒就卷起来，像卷铺盖，比喻被解雇走人。

meaning.en: To take the blame for something one did not do.
meaning.zh: 替别人承担过错或冤枉的责任。

examples.zh: 项目出了问题，却让新来的小李背黑锅。
examples.en: The project went wrong, yet the newcomer Xiao Li was made to take the rap.

examples.zh: 我可不愿意替别人背这口黑锅。
examples.en: I won't take the blame for somebody else.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; often with 替人 or 让…. The soot-covered pot on one's back is an undeserved burden.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“替人背黑锅”。比喻无端承担不属于自己的罪名。

natural: be made to suffer by someone in power

meaning.en: To be quietly treated unfairly or made things hard for by someone with power over you.
meaning.zh: 受有权势的人暗中刁难、打击报复。

examples.zh: 他提了意见以后，经理就总给他穿小鞋。
examples.en: After he raised objections, the manager kept making life difficult for him.

examples.zh: 我怕得罪领导，被穿小鞋。
examples.en: I'm afraid of offending the boss and being given a hard time.

usage.en: Usually 给某人穿小鞋 (to make someone suffer) or 被穿小鞋; used of workplace or hierarchical settings. Shoes that are too tight cause constant pain.
usage.zh: 常说“给某人穿小鞋”或“被穿小鞋”，多用于职场。鞋小夹脚，比喻暗中刁难。

meaning.en: To stay up late at night to work or study.
meaning.zh: 为赶任务或复习，夜里不睡觉工作或学习。

examples.zh: 明天考试，大家都在宿舍里开夜车。
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow and everyone is burning the midnight oil in the dorm.

examples.zh: 为了赶稿子，他连续开了三天夜车。
examples.en: To meet the deadline he stayed up late three nights running.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; used of both work and study. Originally from running extra night trains or night shifts.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，工作学习都可用。本指夜间开车赶运，后指熬夜工作学习。

meaning.en: To be turned down or rebuffed when asking for something.
meaning.zh: 遇到拒绝或受到挫折。

examples.zh: 他去求人帮忙，结果碰了个钉子。
examples.en: He went to ask for help and was rebuffed.

examples.zh: 我去找经理谈加薪，结果碰了钉子。
examples.en: I went to ask the manager for a raise and got rebuffed.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 碰了个钉子. Often paired with 碰一鼻子灰.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“碰了个钉子”，常与“碰一鼻子灰”连用。

meaning.en: Women, regarded as half of society's strength; from the slogan that women hold up half the sky.
meaning.zh: 指妇女，意思是妇女能顶半边天。

equivalents: women who hold up half the sky

examples.zh: 现在很多行业里，女性已经成了半边天。
examples.en: In many fields today women are holding up half the sky.

examples.zh: 妇女能顶半边天，这话一点不假。
examples.en: Women hold up half the sky, and that's quite true.

usage.en: Noun; positive, often in 妇女能顶半边天, a slogan popularised in 1950s China. Used to praise women's contribution.
usage.zh: 名词，褒义，常见于“妇女能顶半边天”，这句口号二十世纪五十年代流行，用来赞扬妇女的作用。

meaning.en: A secure job that one is unlikely to lose, typically in government or state-run organisations.
meaning.zh: 指稳定、不易丢掉的职业。

examples.zh: 她考上了公务员，端上了铁饭碗。
examples.en: She passed the civil service exam and has landed a job for life.

examples.zh: 现在没有哪份工作是真正的铁饭碗了。
examples.en: Nowadays no job is truly secure.

usage.en: Noun; often 端铁饭碗 or 砸铁饭碗 (break the iron rice bowl, i.e. end guaranteed employment). Can be mildly critical of complacency.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“端铁饭碗”“砸铁饭碗”。有时带有批评安于现状的意味。

meaning.en: To overcharge or extort money from someone by taking advantage of them.
meaning.zh: 利用别人的弱点或把柄索取财物，或抬高价钱。

examples.zh: 这家景区餐厅专敲游客的竹杠。
examples.en: The restaurant at this scenic spot is out to fleece tourists.

examples.zh: 出租车司机见我是外地人，想敲我竹杠。
examples.en: The taxi driver saw I was from out of town and tried to rip me off.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; the object can be inserted (敲他竹杠). Said to come from smugglers who were shaken down by officials checking their bamboo poles.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，宾语可插入。相传来自检查竹杠藏私货而借机勒索。

meaning.en: To deliberately say or do the opposite of what someone else says or does.
meaning.zh: 故意说与别人相反的话或做相反的事。

examples.zh: 他总爱跟领导唱反调。
examples.en: He always likes to contradict the boss.

examples.zh: 大家都同意，只有他一个人唱反调。
examples.en: Everyone agreed; only he took the opposite line.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; usually 跟/和某人唱反调.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“跟某人唱反调”。

meaning.en: To discourage someone who is full of enthusiasm.
meaning.zh: 对别人的热情或积极性加以打击。

examples.zh: 大家正兴致勃勃地讨论，你别泼冷水。
examples.en: Everyone is enthusiastically discussing it, so don't pour cold water on it.

examples.zh: 他的话给我们泼了一盆冷水。
examples.en: His words threw cold water on our excitement.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; often 泼了一盆冷水 or 给…泼冷水. Cold water douses the fire of enthusiasm.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“泼了一盆冷水”“给…泼冷水”。冷水浇灭热情。

meaning.en: To flatter someone with excessive praise.
meaning.zh: 给人说奉承的好话。

examples.zh: 你别给我戴高帽了，有话直说吧。
examples.en: Stop flattering me and just say what you want.

examples.zh: 他很会给领导戴高帽子。
examples.en: He's good at buttering up his superiors.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 给某人戴高帽(子). Praise is imagined as a tall hat that makes the wearer proud.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“给某人戴高帽子”。比喻吹捧让人飘飘然。

meaning.en: To fail to turn up for an appointment or break a promise.
meaning.zh: 失约，让对方白等。

examples.zh: 说好七点见面，他却放了我鸽子。
examples.en: We agreed to meet at seven, but he stood me up.

examples.zh: 别放鸽子啊，周末的聚会一定要来。
examples.en: Don't flake on us; be sure to come to the weekend party.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 放某人鸽子. Like a released homing pigeon, the person never comes back.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“放某人鸽子”。鸽子放飞后一去不回，比喻失约。

meaning.en: To rely on past achievements or savings instead of making new efforts.
meaning.zh: 依靠过去的成绩、资历或积蓄过日子，不求进取。

examples.zh: 做企业不能只吃老本，得不断创新。
examples.en: A business can't just live off its past; it must keep innovating.

examples.zh: 他退休后没有收入，只能吃老本。
examples.en: With no income after retiring, he can only live off his savings.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; mostly critical when talking about complacency. 老本 means the original capital.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，多含批评意味。“老本”指原有的本钱。

meaning.en: To make a desperate effort only at the last moment, when it is nearly too late.
meaning.zh: 平时不准备，事到临头才匆忙努力。

examples.zh: 考前才临时抱佛脚，肯定来不及。
examples.en: Cramming right before the exam is bound to be too late.

examples.zh: 平时不烧香，急来抱佛脚。
examples.en: You never burn incense usually, and now you hug the Buddha's feet in a panic.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; commonly 临时抱佛脚. From the saying 平时不烧香，临时抱佛脚.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“临时抱佛脚”。出自俗语“平时不烧香，临时抱佛脚”。

meaning.en: An unexpected winner or a little-known competitor who surprisingly does very well.
meaning.zh: 比赛中出人意料获胜的无名选手，也指突然崭露头角的人。

examples.zh: 这支球队是本届比赛最大的黑马。
examples.en: This team is the biggest dark horse of the tournament.

examples.zh: 没人看好他，结果他成了选举中的黑马。
examples.en: Nobody rated him, yet he became the dark horse of the election.

usage.en: Noun; used in sport, elections, business and exams. Borrowed from the English 'dark horse' in horse racing.
usage.zh: 名词，用于体育、选举、商业、考试等。词义借自英语 dark horse（赛马用语）。

meaning.en: A matchmaker, or anyone who brings two people or parties together.
meaning.zh: 撮合婚姻的人，也指居中牵线的人。

examples.zh: 奶奶热心当红娘，给他介绍了好几个对象。
examples.en: Grandma happily played matchmaker and introduced him to several candidates.

examples.zh: 这次合作多亏了他当红娘。
examples.en: We have him to thank for bringing the two companies together.

usage.en: Noun, often 当红娘. Named after Hongniang, the maid who helps the lovers in the Yuan play 《西厢记》.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“当红娘”。得名于元杂剧《西厢记》中撮合崔莺莺与张生的丫鬟红娘。

meaning.en: A problem that has dragged on for a long time and is hard to solve.
meaning.zh: 指长期存在、难以解决的问题。

examples.zh: 交通拥堵是这座城市的老大难问题。
examples.en: Traffic congestion is this city's chronic problem.

examples.zh: 停车难成了小区的老大难。
examples.en: Parking has become the neighbourhood's perennial headache.

usage.en: Noun, usually 老大难问题; also names the person or unit that everyone finds hard to deal with. Common in news and official writing.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“老大难问题”，也指人人都觉得难办的人或单位。常见于新闻和公文。

meaning.en: To reduce in value or quality; to not be carried out fully.
meaning.zh: 比喻不完全兑现，质量或效果有所降低。

examples.zh: 政策到了基层就打了折扣。
examples.en: The policy was watered down by the time it reached the grassroots.

examples.zh: 这件事要认真做，不能打折扣。
examples.en: Do this seriously; no half measures.

usage.en: Verb-object; besides the literal 'give a discount' it means that quality or effort is reduced. Often 不打折扣 (fully, without compromise).
usage.zh: 动宾短语；除“减价”的本义外，比喻质量或力度打了折。常说“不打折扣”。

meaning.en: A list of people or companies who are banned or disapproved of.
meaning.zh: 记录不良行为者、被禁止或限制者的名单。

examples.zh: 他因为多次违规被列入了黑名单。
examples.en: He was put on the blacklist for repeated violations.

examples.zh: 这家公司已被平台拉进黑名单。
examples.en: The platform has blacklisted this company.

usage.en: Noun; used with 列入/拉入/上. Also used for phone numbers and accounts you block.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“列入黑名单”“上黑名单”，也指手机里被屏蔽的号码、账号。

meaning.en: To be unable to stand something because it is too tiring, heavy or intense.
meaning.zh: 承受不了，负担不起。

examples.zh: 天天加班到半夜，谁也吃不消。
examples.en: Nobody could stand working until midnight every day.

examples.zh: 这么辣的菜，我可吃不消。
examples.en: I can't handle such spicy food.

usage.en: Complement structure; the positive form is 吃得消. Usually negative. Not about eating alone: 消 means to digest or withstand.
usage.zh: 述补结构，肯定式是“吃得消”。多用否定形式，“消”是承受的意思，不限于吃东西。

meaning.en: A long-established shop or brand with a good reputation.
meaning.zh: 历史悠久、信誉良好的商店或品牌。

examples.zh: 这家老字号的点心做了上百年了。
examples.en: This time-honoured shop has been making pastries for over a hundred years.

examples.zh: 北京有不少老字号，比如全聚德。
examples.en: Beijing has many old brands, such as Quanjude.

usage.en: Noun; 字号 is the shop's name or sign. Used for restaurants, medicine shops, tea houses and other traditional businesses.
usage.zh: 名词，“字号”指商店的名称招牌。用于饭馆、药店、茶庄等传统商家。

meaning.en: A very cunning, experienced person who is hard to fool.
meaning.zh: 非常狡猾、经验老到、不易被骗的人。

examples.zh: 他是商场上的老狐狸，谁也骗不了他。
examples.en: He's a sly old fox in business; nobody can fool him.

examples.zh: 别想糊弄那只老狐狸。
examples.en: Don't think you can fool that old fox.

usage.en: Noun, casual; can be admiring or critical, depending on tone. Foxes stand for cunning.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，可褒可贬。狐狸比喻狡猾。

meaning.en: A person with plenty of experience of the world who is not easily fooled.
meaning.zh: 阅历丰富、熟悉世事、不易受骗的人。

examples.zh: 跟老江湖打交道，千万别耍小聪明。
examples.en: When dealing with a seasoned operator, don't try clever tricks.

examples.zh: 他是跑了三十年生意的老江湖。
examples.en: He's an old hand who has been in business for thirty years.

usage.en: Noun; 江湖 is the wider world of wanderers, tradesmen and martial artists. Neutral to mildly wary.
usage.zh: 名词，“江湖”指四处奔走谋生者的社会。中性，略带戒备。

meaning.en: To show off in order to draw attention to oneself.
meaning.zh: 在众人面前表现自己，引人注意。

examples.zh: 他什么场合都爱出风头。
examples.en: He loves to show off on every occasion.

examples.zh: 你别抢着出风头，让别人也说说。
examples.en: Don't hog the limelight; let others speak too.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; often 爱出风头 or 出尽风头. 出尽风头 may be neutral, meaning to steal the show.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“爱出风头”“出尽风头”。“出尽风头”有时是中性的。
